chapter: Growing up in the Brubeck family
title: Dan on the Mexico tour and Iola's fan mail and business work
summary: Dan recalls the wild crowds on the Mexican tour and his mother answering fan mail and building grassroots radio exposure; royalties comment.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Yeah and for me I remember, you know, specific times. Like I went on the road with my dad when he went to Mexico. That was kind of a famous tour. And actually Monk was on that tour and I guess it was a George Wein festival that went all over the place. And just, you know, being in these huge auditoriums and seeing people really going nuts, like literally picking up a row of chairs and smashing them down and you’re going whoa. I mean people were really going crazy like it was a soccer game or something. That was the first time I went, “Oh, like these guys are really like big stars” you know. It had never occurred to me of course it was a different kind of mentality in a different country. But the other thing that I — made me recognize the business aspect of it would be you know coming home from school or something and seeing my mom sitting at a desk and going through fan mail and just she constantly worked at stuff. And they answered every bit of mail and sent out records to people. They were very constant, consistent with their you know, keeping the grass roots thing. Because my mom started out, she was actually in a radio station and long ago she kind of figured out the whole Grateful Dead model. You know go to all the radio stations and let them record the group playing, and have them © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

just, give them the rights to just put it out there and it will take — you know more people will hear the band. She was really business oriented and kind of opened tons of doors. But just seeing her at work like that, that’s when I realized the other side of it. I recognized the creative part of it, and that’s the attraction. And then you go okay but there is like a lot of work involved in this too. It’s just doesn’t happen if you’re a creative person. You have to be able to go out there and really work for it.
Yeah, and over the years as Dave wrote more and had more LPs out, keeping track of royalties and are we getting a fair-square deal here and all that.
And of course they weren’t because they were the artists.
